Nagydobos Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nagydobos, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews first settled in Nagydobos in the first half of the 19th century, mostly as petty traders; a synagogue built in 1830 marked the community's independence, though it joined Mátészalka's jurisdiction by 1885. Population peaked at 237 by 1910, declining to 148 by 1941; Rabbi David Jungreiz, also head of the rabbinical court in Nyírmeggyes, led the community. In April 1944, residents were imprisoned in the synagogue for three days without food before transfer to the Mátészalka Ghetto (which held 18,000 Jews from the district) and deportation to Auschwitz by month's end; no Jews returned to Nagydobos after the war. This cemetery appears on an 1891 cadastral map, with its newest tombstone dated 1939.
